name: cml-driver-eye-realmux
description: sim/cml-driver-eye's graded driver rows -- DR-0002's single-ended swing and common-mode windows, spec/tmds-tx.md #2's <= 0.15 UI jitter allocation, the tail-current window and the device-stress ceilings -- re-measured with the REAL DR-0003 final multiplexer (design/tmds_final_mux.sch) substituted for the ideal differential source those records model it as. Same driver cell, same DR-0002 load, same 0/1/2 pF in-deck pad-capacitance sweep, same leg-mismatch and termination-rail sensitivity copies, same measurement windows, same full PVT x bit-rate grid. Does NOT supersede sim/cml-driver-eye: it is a second, harder experiment on the same cell (jitter is referenced to the ideal clock, so it is the mux-plus-driver contribution, not the driver's alone).
claim: spec/tmds-tx.md#dr-0002 -- single-ended swing 400-600 mV and common mode 2.8-3.3 V into 50 ohm/leg with a ~10 mA tail, plus the Vgs/Vgd/Vds margin against the 3.3 V core devices' rated limit -- and spec/tmds-tx.md #2's remaining-jitter row (<= 0.15 UI peak-to-peak), at both #1 operating points, now with the DR-0003 multiplexer's REAL output rather than the ideal-source assumption design/cml-driver-sizing.md section 4.1 levied on it.

transient.pattern: mixed-run-length-16b (1111111110101010, MSB first at t=0) -- the same output pattern sim/cml-driver-eye drives, synthesised through the half-rate DDR mux from a constant D0 word and a single-transition D1 word

swing_c0.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV, 0 pF pad -- same definition, window and comb as sim/cml-driver-eye's row of the same name, with the ideal input source replaced by the real DR-0003 multiplexer.

swing_c1.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV, 1 pF pad, real mux input

swing_c2.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV at DR-0005's full 2 pF pad-capacitance budget, real mux input

vcm_c0.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V, 0 pF pad, at the nominal 3.3 V receiver termination rail (avcc -10 %/+10 % sensitivity reported separately as vcm_avcclo/vcm_avcchi), real mux input

vcm_c1.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V, 1 pF pad, real mux input

vcm_c2.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V at DR-0005's full 2 pF budget, real mux input

dj_ui_c0.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row, 0 pF pad. Referenced to the ideal half-rate CLOCK, so this is the MUX-PLUS-DRIVER deterministic jitter, not the driver's alone -- strictly harder than sim/cml-driver-eye's row of the same name, and the number that actually maps onto #2's allocation for this block. Random jitter is not a transient quantity and is not included.

dj_ui_c1.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row, 1 pF pad, mux-plus-driver

dj_ui_c2.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row at DR-0005's full 2 pF budget, mux-plus-driver

dj_ui_cmis.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row with a deliberate 1 pF leg-to-leg pad-capacitance mismatch (2 pF on OUTP, 1 pF on OUTN), mux-plus-driver

swing_cmis.description: DR-0002 swing under the same 1 pF leg-to-leg pad mismatch, real mux input

vgs_sw_max.description: Switching-device Vgs against the 3.3 V core devices' rated terminal voltage, adopting the identical 3.63 V ceiling and citation sim/cml-driver-eye's own row of this name uses. Measured on the avcc +10 % copy; the gate node is now the real mux output rather than an ideal source.

vgd_sw_max.description: Switching-device |Vgd| against the same 3.63 V rated limit -- the binding stress row, since the off device's gate sits at the multiplexer's low level while its drain is pulled to the termination rail

vds_sw_max.description: Switching-device Vds against the same 3.63 V rated limit

vgs_tail_max.description: Tail/mirror-device Vgs (the shared bias node) against the same 3.63 V rated limit

vds_tail_max.description: Tail-device Vds (the tail node) against the same 3.63 V rated limit

itail_dc.description: Tail current from the ideal 500 uA reference through the cell's 1:20 mirror, with the driver's inputs now at the real mux's DC levels. The 8-12 mA window is design/cml-driver-sizing.md's derived tail-current tolerance; a real mux that under-drives the switch pair shows up here as a tail current the termination cannot account for.

ui_ref.description: Harness-integrity check, not a design claim: the measured unit interval must differ by more than 50 % across the grid, which it can only do if rate_val actually reached the stimulus.
